subject: science
domain: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

items.prompt:
Sugar molecules contain
A) carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen
B) only iron
C) only salt
D) only water

steps: Sugars contain carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.

items.prompt:
To build amino acids, which element is added?
A) Nitrogen
B) Gold
C) Helium
D) Neon

Amino acids join to form
A) proteins
B) water
C) rocks
D) oxygen

steps: Proteins are built from amino acids.

items.prompt:
Carbon can form many large molecules because it
A) can bond to several atoms and form chains and rings
B) never bonds
C) is a metal
D) is a gas only
items.answer: A) can bond to several atoms and form chains and rings

items.prompt:
The carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen in an organism come mainly from
A) rocks
B) sugars made in photosynthesis
C) metal
D) salt

Which is a large carbon-based molecule in living things?
A) A protein
B) Table salt
C) Water
D) Oxygen gas

steps: Proteins are carbon-based molecules of life.

items.prompt:
How does an organism build a protein from sugar?
A) It uses carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen from sugar, adds nitrogen to make amino acids, and joins them into a protein
B) It uses only oxygen
C) It cannot build proteins
D) It uses only salt
items.answer: A) It uses carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen from sugar, adds nitrogen to make amino acids, and joins them into a protein

steps: Sugar atoms plus nitrogen form amino acids, then proteins.

items.prompt:
All of life's large molecules contain carbon because carbon
A) forms the backbone chains that hold the molecules together
B) is a metal
C) never bonds
D) is radioactive
items.answer: A) forms the backbone chains that hold the molecules together

steps: Carbon chains form the backbone of these molecules.
